title: Dessert disguised itself as asparagus
hook: That vegetable on the dessert plate could be ice cream in disguise
summary: Historical ice cream molds made shapes such as asparagus and fish. This is a story about vegetable shapes, not confirmed vegetable flavors.

text: Asparagus on the dessert plate? Historical ice creams could pull off that disguise.
Cook Agnes Marshall described and sold dessert molds shaped like asparagus, fish and swans.

panels.text: I was already bracing myself for vegetables.

text: Ice cream was packed into molds to give it shape. The photo shows several designs from Marshall's book.
History museums recreate these desserts, too. Briefly dipping the mold in warm water helps release the ice cream.
Asparagus-shaped isn't the same as asparagus-flavored. What the records confirm here is the mold and its shape.

panels.text: Even ice cream gets a vegetable costume.
